title: 48/60 NANOROBOT-ASSISTED AUTONOMOUS REPAIR OF REGENERATIVE BIOMATERIALS AT THE LIMIT NANOROBOT-ASSISTED AUTONOMOUS REPAIR OF REGENERATIVE BIOMATERIALS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 48/60). It investigates material fracture recovery versus concealed residual damage. The research coupling is biomaterial defect detection x local microrobotic repair x independent function requalification. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: An independently tested local repair policy will recover preregistered mechanical performance while preserving cells, unlike appearance-only recovery. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-seed gel cracks and delaminations, then compare robot patching, manual repair and full replacement. Strong comparators include expert adhesive gel patching, replacement and monitored no-repair. A central rival account is lowered post-repair acceptance thresholds or hidden damage reclassified as healed. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: hidden cracks, cell injury or post-repair fatigue worsen. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020.
